newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico clears way for private petrochemical plants.
newsitem.headline: Mexico clears way for private petrochemical plants.

text.p: The Mexican government on Friday laid the foundations in its Official Gazette for the spinning off of its second and third largest petrochemical plants.
The plants, La Cangrejera and Morelos in Veracruz state, are set to be established as subsidiaries of state oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex), it said.

The disincorporation announced Friday is an initial step toward the government's sale of a minority ownership in the plants to private companies. Currently Pemex owns the nation's 10 petrochemical complexes.
Cangrejera produced 3.72 million tonnes and Morelos 1.61 million tonnes of petrochemicals in 1994.
The privatization is expected to begin in August, Energy Minister Jesus Reyes Heroles has said.

Four of the plants have already been established as subsidiary companies of Pemex, and the remaining six -- including La Cangrejera and Morelos -- will be set up by mid-year, ministry officials have said.
